submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole fires where a quantity or measure expression is attached to what it quantifies: its strongest activations (up to ~2.2 against a 0.18 corpus mean) are on the partitive ' of' after a numeral or measure word - percentages ('90% of', '90 percent of'), counts and durations ('20 years of', '10 minutes of'), and magnitude words ('thousands of', 'millions of') - and it also fires on a noun directly quantified by a preceding numeral ('20,000 people', '216 tree populations'). The response is graded: quantifier words ('most of', 'half of') and a descriptive adjective before a concrete noun ('big house', 'enlarged liver') give weaker versions, while genitive ' of' after an ordinary noun ('the capital of France', 'the end of the story') and nouns preceded directly by a plain determiner stay at baseline.

The Riverton water utility published its annual report on Monday, and the findings drew immediate attention from the town council. According to the document, the treatment plant processed a daily average that has climbed steadily since the filtration upgrade was completed in 2019. Engineers credited the improvement to new membranes installed along the eastern intake, which reduced sediment loads and cut the frequency of emergency shutdowns. The report also notes that maintenance costs rose faster than revenue, leaving a shortfall that the council will need to address before the next fiscal year. The document includes lengthy appendices on water quality sampling and on the cost of replacing aging pumps.

Residents who attended the public meeting raised questions about the taste of the water and the condition of the pipes beneath the older neighbourhoods. One speaker described brown discolouration appearing after heavy rain, a problem the utility attributed to iron sediment dislodged when pressure fluctuates. Staff said flushing crews have been dispatched to the affected streets twice already this spring and will continue through the summer.

The utility's customer assistance program enrolled more households than expected, though staff acknowledged that outreach has been uneven across the service area. Community groups have offered to distribute notices in several languages and to host drop-in sessions at the library, where residents can ask about payment plans and conservation rebates.

The council asked for a clearer timeline for replacing the lead service lines that remain in parts of the downtown core. Utility managers replied that the inventory is not yet complete, and that the work will depend on state grants. They estimated that 42% of the remaining lines run beneath private property, which complicates access and raises costs for homeowners. Several council members pressed for a map showing where the lines are located, arguing that residents deserve to know whether their homes are affected.

A separate section of the report addresses the reservoir on the northern ridge. Its capacity has shrunk because of siltation, and the utility has commissioned a study to evaluate dredging. The study is expected to run for more than a year and will consider the effect on downstream habitats, including a wetland that supports several rare plants. Conservation groups have asked to be included in the review, noting that the reservoir feeds a creek where trout spawn each autumn.

Two council members also asked whether the utility could publish monthly water quality results online, rather than only in the annual report. Managers said a dashboard is under development and should be available by the end of the year, pending a review of the software vendor's security practices.

Near the end of the meeting, the utility's finance director presented a long-range projection showing modest rate increases and a plan to borrow for the replacement of a pump station built in the 1950s. He warned that deferring the work would raise the risk of a failure during peak summer demand, when the system already runs close to its limit. The council voted to schedule a follow-up session and asked staff to bring cost estimates and a list of grant programs that might share the burden.
